subject: Order form: invoicing cadence, minimum commit & tax allocation
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah@cerebellum.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cerebellum.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form: invoicing cadence, minimum commit & tax allocation

Hi Jonas / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Cerebellum is excited to move forward. Before we sign the Order Form we have two operational items procurement asked us to confirm so our AP team can map the invoice flow:

- Invoice cadence: our preference is quarterly invoices, but we can accept monthly if the minimum commit is split. Can you confirm Redwood's default cadence and flexibility?
- Minimum commit phasing: can the committed amount be invoiced in two tranches (50/50 or 60/40)? We need this for cash flow planning.
- Net terms: Cerebellum operates on Net 45. Is Net 45 acceptable or will you require Net 30? If Net 45 is an exception, what approvals or fees apply?
- Taxes: we operate in the US entity and will supply tax residency evidence. We need clarity on whether Redwood will gross-up for withholding or if we need to provide a W-8/W-9 equivalent. Also confirm whether Redwood will accept our VAT/exempt certificate for EU billing if needed later.

Procurement would like a redlined Order Form and a one-page invoice schedule we can attach to the PO. Can you send a proposed split and the doc we should sign?

Thanks,
Sarah Park
VP Finance, Cerebellum Labs

---
Attachments: none
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@cerebellum.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Apr 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: invoicing cadence, minimum commit & tax allocation

Hi Sarah — quick answers and next steps.

Thanks for raising these; happy to get procurement a concise packet. Summary below:

- Default cadence: Redwood issues monthly invoices by default. Monthly gives cleaner usage reconciliation.
- Flexibility: we can accommodate quarterly invoicing for committed dollars only, but for usage overages we still invoice monthly (or at the end of the quarter with line-item detail).
- Minimum commit phasing: we typically support a two-tranche model. Common splits are 60/40 or 50/50. For large commits we can do 30/70 with draft approval from finance.
- Net terms: our standard is Net 30. We can approve Net 45 for strategic accounts on an exceptions basis (requires finance sign-off). There is no automatic fee, but we do ask for a commitment to the two-tranche structure for longer Net terms.
- Taxes: we need a certificate of tax residency (W-9 or W-8BEN-E as applicable) and will apply tax treatment per the invoicing entity and jurisdiction. Redwood does not gross-up for customer withholding by default; if the customer requires gross-up we need to document it in the Order Form (gross-up language or tax grossing clause).

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben, can you assemble a commercial proposal (two-tranche split + suggested Net 45 approval path) and attach a redline of the Order Form we want Cerebellum to sign?
2) Lauren, can you confirm any finance pre-approval criteria for Net 45 (credit check / deal size threshold)?
3) Kimberly, we'd appreciate a quick legal read on any escrow/withholding language that might be required.

Sarah — I'll follow up with a redline and an invoice schedule PDF that you can attach to the PO.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form: invoicing cadence, minimum commit & tax allocation

Hi all — attaching a proposed commercial compromise for Cerebellum (deal id RWI-2025-97431). Key commercial points in the redline (attached):

- Commit split: 60% invoiced at execution, 40% invoiced 90 days after commencement. This keeps cash runway visible to both teams.
- Invoice cadence: committed amounts billed per tranche; any overages billed monthly and reconciled each quarter.
- Net terms: accept Net 45 for the first 12 months for this deal, subject to finance sign-off (Lauren, please confirm). After 12 months account reverts to Net 30 unless an extension is agreed.
- Taxes: customer to provide tax residency form within 10 business days of execution. In the absence of valid residency evidence, Redwood will withhold applicable taxes per jurisdiction and will notify Cerebellum. If Cerebellum requests gross-up, legal must approve language and finance must model impact.

I have attached: OrderForm_Cereb_redline_v1.pdf (redline of pricing appendix + payment section) and a one-page invoice schedule PDF (InvoiceSchedule_Cereb_v1.pdf).

Requesting: Kimberly — please confirm whether the withholding/gross-up paragraph below is materially acceptable or if legal will need to propose alternative language.

Proposed withholding paragraph (commercial placeholder):
"If Customer is legally required to withhold taxes on payments to Redwood, Customer shall remit such withheld amounts to the appropriate authorities and provide Redwood with evidence of remittance and any certificates of tax residency. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, prices are not grossed up for withholding taxes."

Lauren — can you confirm Net 45 exception criteria?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form: invoicing cadence, minimum commit & tax allocation

Thanks Ben — I reviewed the redline and attached a tracked-changes version. High-level legal notes:

- Withholding language: the proposed commercial placeholder is fine as a starting point. Legal recommends adding: (a) a mechanism for Redwood to request documentary evidence of remittance if withholding is applied; and (b) an express statement that Redwood will cooperate with reasonable documentary requests.
- Gross-up: we generally avoid automatic gross-up clauses. If Cerebellum insists on a gross-up, require finance to include a line item in the Order Form to cover estimated additional cost and add an explicit cap/renewal review.
- Escrow/credit: for Net 45 approval we prefer a credit-review workflow (Lauren to confirm). If finance requires, we can add an escrow clause for committed dollars only — operationally this is heavier and typically reserved for multi-year prepay deals.
- Invoice schedule: the attached tracked PDF includes a one-page schedule template; remove the "overage reconciliation" language from the front page and place it in section 3 to keep the PO short.

I attached: OrderForm_Cereb_redline_tracked.pdf (tracked changes), and a short checklist for procurement (Procurement_Checklist_stub.pdf).

If Sarah is comfortable with the 60/40 and Net 45-for-12-months approach I think we can move to DocuSign next week. Otherwise flag which items require alternate language.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
